title: Inference-context-matched, format-controlled evaluation with a training-free context baseline
description: Redesign the evaluation so that the supervision regime is not confounded with the inference-time context. Evaluate every trained model under the same test-time context (both no-context and context-provided settings), add a training-free context baseline and a KG-neighborhood baseline at matched token budget, use byte-identical templates across arms, and score with a format-controlled metric that cannot be affected by the grounding instruction.
why_differs: Existing systems measure context effects only at inference, and existing training works do not hold inference context constant across arms. This modification makes the training-time claim separable from the dominant inference-time paradigm (the exact gap G001).
technical_mechanism: Fix the inference-time prompt to include a specified context for all models (and repeat with none), so the only difference between the compared models is their training supervision. Use identical templates and a scorer that extracts the answer rather than judging response format.
expected_benefit: Makes the central claim identifiable: it distinguishes 'learning to use context' from 'being given context at test time', and it answers U010 directly instead of leaving it as an assumption. If the training-time effect disappears once inference context is controlled, the paper reports that cleanly rather than overclaiming.
potential_novelty: Hedged: the evaluation protocol (training effect measured under matched inference context with a shuffled-context control) was not found in the retrieved literature and would be a reusable methodological contribution independent of the outcome.
implementation_difficulty_basis: Prompting and scoring changes only; the training-free baseline can reuse an existing GraphRAG-style pipeline.
experimental_difficulty_basis: Requires running each trained model under several inference-context conditions, plus a training-free baseline and a format-controlled scorer; it multiplies evaluation runs but needs no new training method.
main_risk: A format-controlled scorer may itself be less sensitive, potentially washing out real effects; this must be reported with a sensitivity analysis rather than hidden.
required_baselines: Training-free context baseline (Co-E-style / GraphRAG) at matched budget
No-context and context-provided test-time conditions for every trained model
